title: Grenzbefestigung Altfinstermünz
highlights: Medieval border fortress and customs outpost deep inside the Inn River gorge
Spectacular wooden bridge featuring a fortified defense tower spanning the raging Inn
Historic Sigmundseck hermitage gatehouse and mysterious cave fortress set into the cliff
Crucial ancient transit checkpoint along the Roman Via Claudia Augusta
kurzbeschreibung: Altfinstermünz is a medieval border and customs fortress nestled deep in the Inn Gorge, complete with wooden bridge and cave castle.
beschreibung:
Medieval Customs Station in the Innschlucht

Altfinstermünz lies deep in the dramatic rock canyon of the Inn on the border between Tirol and Graubünden. Travellers crossed this crucial bottleneck along the Via Claudia Augusta as early as Roman times, before Duke Sigmund der Münzreiche commissioned the present-day fortification in the 15th century.

Defensive Tower, Bridge, and Cave Chapel

The site comprises a fortified bridge tower standing right in the river, the Klause Sigmundseck gatehouse, and a mysterious cave fortress built into the sheer rock wall. A meticulously restored discovery trail with a suspension bridge and historical information panels brings this adventurous era of trade and customs controls vividly to life.
